item: A ratchet classifies every loop in src/database whose back-edge sits outside the cleanup around it; two of them were reachable from a main thread and are converted; two comments stop attaching a timing to a phase
refs: PR #1501; audit 0.5.0 A-012 part 2 and A-027; follows PR #1489 and R234
summary: A-012 part 2: tests/test_database_loop_heads_are_classified.py lists the ten scopes in src/database whose loop back-edge lies outside an enclosing with, try/finally or except BaseException/KeyboardInterrupt, each with who runs it (worker-only or event-loop), and fails on a new such head without a row and on a stale row; rows are keyed by qualified name, module and class bodies count, only the body of a with/try counts, and an anti-vacuity test pins the shapes it reads. The review of the first draft found two rows wrong: corpus_lease.active_leases is reached on a main thread by src/monitoring/release_run_fresh_restore.py (run_restore -> wait_for_quiescence, a subprocess in the server's process group), and pool_watch._live_rows by whatever thread times out on a pool checkout; both loops are converted to the guard-clause form and removed from the table (behaviour unchanged, harm today near nil: that child exits). The worker-only classification of the ten that remain rests on callers found by grep, not on thread starts traced line by line (inferred, labelled so in the test); a row covers its whole function, so a new loop added to a listed function passes unseen, and tests/test_worker_only_callers_pinned.py is the stronger check for the two functions it pins. A-027: two fts.py comments said 981 s then 1,645 s on a 130 GB corpus for the FTS rebuild; SCALE_ROADMAP P0.4 records the unlock as a whole (two consecutive boots on 2026-07-09, database 11.7 GB / 268,241 articles) and does not split it by phase, the data folder size is unidentified there, and the rebuild as cause was fixed against a synthetic corpus only (shipped.csv 2026-07-10, awaiting live validation), so the comments now say that. Comment-only apart from the two loop conversions.
